subject: Materials Science
title: Natural Composites: Wood and Bone
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Natural Composites: Wood and Bone.

hook.text: Your thighbone supports ten times your body weight — it's nature's carbon fiber.

buildup.text: Bone is collagen fibers (tough and flexible) reinforced with hydroxyapatite crystals (hard).

discovery.text: Wood is cellulose fibers in a lignin matrix — strong along the grain, weak across it.

twist.text: Bone remodels itself — it adds material where stress is high and removes it where stress is low.

climax.text: Engineers study bone and wood to design self-optimizing, lightweight synthetic composites.

punchline.text: Nature engineered composites billions of years before we did.

quiz.question: What makes bone a composite material?
options: It is made of pure calcium
It combines flexible collagen with hard hydroxyapatite
It contains air bubbles for lightness
